title: Executive leadership
description: Compare strategic options, their use of limited resources and the risks an executive must decide whether to accept.
questions: Which strategic objective does this decision serve, and what would change if the current approach continued?
What investment or team capacity must the decision maker reserve, and which existing work would give way?
Who can commit those resources or accept the remaining risk, and what evidence would make them revisit the decision?

sources.title: HM Treasury, Developing business cases for projects and programmes
Kaplan and Norton, The Balanced Scorecard, measures that drive performance

specialists.title: Strategic fit
specialists.focus: Compare the change with current objectives and identify which intended result the proposal can affect.

specialists.title: Portfolio and resources
specialists.focus: Check the full demands on funds and people, including recurring costs and any work that loses resources.

specialists.title: Risk and decision rights
specialists.focus: Identify approvals and trade-offs that exceed the sponsor's authority or the organization's documented risk appetite.

specialists.title: Benefits tracking
specialists.focus: Test whether the proposed measures track the intended result and name who will compare them with the current baseline.

evidence: Read the latest authorized strategy and its measurable objectives. Check which of them the proposal affects and how.
Compare the current approach with viable alternatives using the same categories of cost, people, expected outcomes and timing.
Check the approved risk thresholds, budget limits and delegated authority with the relevant owners. Record gaps without copying confidential board material.
Identify who produced each forecast, when it was last updated and what observation would test its most consequential assumption.
challenge: Test one realistic scenario where adoption is slower, benefits are lower or costs are higher. Identify any option that would then rank higher.
Check whether one option appears attractive because the analysis omitted displaced work, organizational change or ongoing support.
Distinguish a decision the sponsor can reverse from a commitment that requires a governing body or formal approval.
Which measure would show within the first months that the decision is not producing the expected result?
decision_criteria: Present the current approach and viable alternatives against one strategic objective and a consistent evidence-based comparison.
Make the opportunity cost, remaining risks and unresolved assumptions visible to the person with authority to decide.
For the recommended option, name the result owner and the date or threshold for expanding, pausing or revisiting the commitment.
Escalate to the governing body any commitment that exceeds the delegated budget, risk appetite or duration.
